findings.evidence: Page 46 (§2.1.2, 'What Actually Happens During Inference'): "In whole-clip latent video generation, a prompt conditions repeated updates to a space-time tensor. One denoising step can process the entire current clip representation. A later VAE decoder maps the final representation into frames. Its name, 'decode,' does not make it the single-token decode loop in Fig 2.1. [1P][FACT] (Wan2.2 sampling loop, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28 — post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028, outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff.)"
findings.issue: Evidence-label/provenance defect: the sentence states a [1P][FACT] claim (Wan2.2 whole-clip denoising behaviour, and specifically that a later VAE decoder maps the final representation into frames) with no first-party source identified in the sentence — no paper, model card, repository, or datasheet is named. The only pointer is a bare git revision hash ('pinned revision 1ea34ff'), which is not a resolvable source identifier for a reader, and the same passage later says the source establishes 'the execution pattern below' while the VAE-decoder claim is an additional factual assertion not covered by that pattern statement. Compare with the book-wide convention elsewhere (e.g. Ch 1's model cards cited as 'HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next', Ch 7's 'GGUF specification, pinned revision, retrieved 2026-10-28' naming the spec). A [1P][FACT] label requires a named first-party source per the Preface evidence discipline; a revision hash with no repository/URL/file path cannot be resolved by a reader.
findings.fix_instruction: Name the first-party source explicitly for the Wan2.2 sampling-loop claim (e.g. 'Wan2.2 technical report / model card, HF Wan-AI/... , pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28') or downgrade the label to [1P][DERIVED]/[ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] with the reasoning made explicit. If the VAE-decoder sentence cannot be traced to the same pinned source, split it out and give it its own named source or label.

findings.evidence: Page 53: "Decode: required bandwidth, hypothetical single-device aggregate (TPOT ~25 ms) | 5.6 TB/s | 140 GB / 0.025 s — the whole model read once per step on one device (batch-1-equivalent weight-streaming model, before amortization); an aggregate figure, not a per-GPU one [canonical scenario][DERIVED]"
findings.issue: Arithmetic/unit inconsistency across chapters: the 140 GB / 0.025 s figure is quoted with a [canonical scenario][DERIVED] label and with a 25 ms TPOT denominator, but 25 ms is not a canonical-scenario input for this computation — it is the canonical TPOT budget of 25 ms/token, which is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] (Table 4-2, 'Decode (TPOT) | 25 ms/token | [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]'), so the derived value inherits an assumed denominator. More materially, the same page states the aggregate figure is 'the whole model read once per step on one device' and then Table 2-2's next row (page 54) computes the 'required bandwidth per GPU (sharded, TP = 8) | 700 GB/s per GPU | 17.5 GB / 0.025 s' — so the chapter carries two different 'required bandwidth' numbers (5.6 TB/s vs 700 GB/s) for the same canonical step, differing by 8×, and the 5.6 TB/s figure is repeatedly quoted in later chapters (Ch 3 mini-case, Ch 6 Table 6-1 '~140 GB weight-read → ~5.6 TB/s rate (batch-1-equivalent)') as if it were the workload's bandwidth demand. The chapter does hedge it, but the labelling and the repeated quotation make the hypothetical single-device number read as a canonical demand. The arithmetic itself (140/0.025 = 5,600 GB/s; 17.5/0.025 = 700 GB/s) is correct; the defect is the label/quotation framing that lets a hypothetical figure carry canonical-scenario authority in three chapters.
findings.fix_instruction: Either relabel the 5.6 TB/s row as [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] (a hypothetical single-device illustration, not the canonical scenario's demand) or add an explicit '[canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] denominator: TPOT 25 ms' note to the row. Where Ch 6 Table 6-1 and the Ch 3 mini-case quote '5.6 TB/s', add the same single-device/hypothetical qualifier at the point of quotation so the number cannot be read as the canonical host's demand.
